The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Let $(\Theta,\mathcal T)$, $(\mathsf X,\mathcal A)$, and
$(\mathsf Z,\mathcal C)$ be measurable spaces (sets equipped with
sigma-algebras; [[def-measurable-space]]). Let $\nu$ and $\mu$ be sigma-finite
reference measures on the observation and latent spaces; each has a countable
measurable cover by sets of finite measure
([[def-finite-sigma-finite-and-semifinite-measures]]). The finite product
sigma-algebra is generated by measurable rectangles
([[def-product-sigma-algebra-and-finite-product-sigma-algebras]]). The product
reference measure $\nu\otimes\mu$ is the one supplied by
[[thm-sigma-finite-product-measure-exists-is-rectangular-and-is-unique]].

A **jointly measurable latent-variable density** is a specified function
$$ p:\Theta\times\mathsf X\times\mathsf Z\longrightarrow[0,\infty] $$
measurable for $\mathcal T\otimes\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal C$ and normalized
on every parameter fibre:
$$ \int_{\mathsf X\times\mathsf Z}p(\theta,x,z)\, (\nu\otimes\mu)(d(x,z))=1\qquad(\theta\in\Theta). $$
Here $x$ is the observed coordinate and $z$ the latent coordinate. The
observed marginal density is
$$ m(\theta,x):=\int_{\mathsf Z}p(\theta,x,z)\,\mu(dz). $$
The valid-fibre set is
$V:=\{(\theta,x):0<m(\theta,x)<\infty\}$. Only on $V$ define the normalized
latent-fibre density
$$ q(z\mid\theta,x):=\frac{p(\theta,x,z)}{m(\theta,x)}. $$
This definition requires a single jointly measurable density as an input.
[[def-likelihood-density]] supplies neither a sigma-algebra on $\Theta$ nor
joint parameter measurability from separately specified likelihood sections;
the joint measurability above is an additional hypothesis. Because $p$ is
already supplied as one joint function, this definition uses no choice axiom.
It does not assert that AC can turn separately specified pointwise likelihood
versions into a jointly measurable version. No quotient or pointwise
conditional density is asserted on a zero or infinite marginal fibre.

Let $\mathcal E=((\mathcal X,\mathcal A),\Theta,(P_\theta)_{\theta\in\Theta})$
be dominated by the fixed sigma-finite positive measure $\mu$. For each
$\theta$, the Radon–Nikodym theorem gives the almost-everywhere class
$dP_\theta/d\mu$; a sigma-finite exhaustion for $\mu$ is also finite for the
probability measure $P_\theta$. Under AC, select simultaneously a
finite-valued measurable nonnegative representative $p_\theta$ from each
class. The nonnegative version exists by
[[lem-radon-nikodym-density-of-a-finite-positive-measure-has-a-nonnegative-representative]].

For fixed observed $x\in\mathcal X$, the function
$$L_x:\Theta\to[0,+\infty),\qquad L_x(\theta):=p_\theta(x),$$
is the **likelihood at $x$**. This is a function on the parameter labels, not
a probability distribution on $\Theta$. No sigma-algebra on $\Theta$ or
measurability of $L_x$ is implied. Each density is determined only
$\mu$-almost everywhere; there is no canonical pointwise version and, for
arbitrary uncountable $\Theta$, no common exceptional null set is asserted.

Assume the hypotheses of
[[def-latent-variable-joint-and-observed-data-factorization]]. Then
$m(\theta,x)=\int p(\theta,x,z)\,\mu(dz)$ is jointly measurable in
$(\theta,x)$. For each fixed $\theta$, it is an observed-data probability
density: it is $\mathcal A$-measurable and
$$ \int_{\mathsf X}m(\theta,x)\,\nu(dx)=1. $$
Consequently $m(\theta,x)<\infty$ for $\nu$-almost every $x$. On every valid
fibre $0<m(\theta,x)<\infty$, $q(z\mid\theta,x)=p(\theta,x,z)/m(\theta,x)$ is
a measurable $\mu$-density of total mass one. Finally, if $h:\Theta\times\mathsf X\times\mathsf Z\to\mathbb C$ is product
measurable and
$\int |h(\theta,x,z)|p(\theta,x,z)\,d(\nu\otimes\mu)<\infty$ for a fixed
$\theta$, Fubini permits exchanging the latent and observed integrals of
$hp$. No exchange is claimed without this absolute integrability.

Let $(E,\mathcal S,\mu)$ and $(T,\mathcal T,\nu)$ be sigma-finite measure spaces. Let a joint probability $\lambda$ on $E\times T$ have nonnegative product-measurable density $p:E\times T\to[0,\infty]$ relative to $\mu\times\nu$. A fixed probability $\rho$ on $(E,\mathcal S)$ is supplied. Put
$$m(y)=\int_E p(x,y)\,\mu(dx),\qquad D=\{y:0<m(y)<\infty\},$$
$$K(y,A)=\begin{cases}\displaystyle\frac{\int_Ap(x,y)\,\mu(dx)}{m(y)},&y\in D,\\ \rho(A),&y\notin D.\end{cases}$$

Then K is an everywhere probability kernel from T to E. If $\beta$ is the second marginal of $\lambda$, then $\beta(D)=1$ and
$$\lambda(A\times B)=\int_B K(y,A)\,\beta(dy).$$

For any random elements X,Y with joint law $\lambda$, $K(Y,\cdot)$ is a regular conditional distribution of X given $\sigma(Y)$. These event identities require no AC. If interpreted with the library's conditional-expectation class existence convention, assume AC. Neither zero nor infinite marginal-density fibres are normalized by the displayed quotient.

Assume AC for the supplied existence theorem. Write $E[X\mid\mathcal G]$ for the unique class in $L^1(\Omega,\mathcal G,P|_{\mathcal G})$ consisting of conditional-expectation versions of $X$. A chosen real $\mathcal G$-measurable representative is a **version**. Equalities and inequalities involving these classes mean almost-sure equalities and inequalities.

Existence is [[thm-conditional-expectation-exists-by-radon-nikodym]] and uniqueness is [[lem-conditional-expectation-is-unique-almost-surely]], applied to [[def-conditional-expectation-given-a-sigma-algebra]]. The quotient is [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]. If $X=X^{\ast}$ almost surely, [[thm-the-lebesgue-integral-respects-almost-everywhere-equality]] gives identical event integrals, so the output class is independent of the input representative. The [[def-axiom-of-choice]] assumption is inherited from RN existence.
Assume AC. For every real integrable $X$ on $(\Omega,\mathcal F,P)$ and every sub-sigma-algebra $\mathcal G$, a conditional-expectation version of $X$ given $\mathcal G$ exists.

Assume AC. If $\phi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is finite convex and both $X$ and $\phi(X)$ are integrable, then $\phi(E[X\mid\mathcal G])\le E[\phi(X)\mid\mathcal G]$ almost surely; the left side is measurable and integrable.

Let $P,Q$ be probability measures on the same measurable space
([[def-probability-measure]]). Absolute continuity $P\ll Q$ has the convention
of [[def-absolutely-continuous-with-respect-to-a-positive-measure]]. If
$P\not\ll Q$, define $D(P\|Q)=+\infty$. If $P\ll Q$, assume AC
([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as in [[def-likelihood-ratio-as-rn-derivative]] and
let $r=dP/dQ$ be a finite-valued nonnegative measurable representative of its
Radon–Nikodym class; such a representative exists by
[[lem-radon-nikodym-density-of-a-finite-positive-measure-has-a-nonnegative-representative]].
On $\{r=0\}$ set $\ell=0$, and on $\{r>0\}$ set $\ell=\log r$. This
function is measurable: for $a\ge0$, $\{\ell>a\}=\{r>\exp(a)\}$, and for
$a<0$, $\{\ell>a\}=\{r=0\}\cup\{r>\exp(a)\}$, by the inverse and
monotonicity properties of the natural logarithm
([[def-natural-logarithm]], [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]). These are
measurable sets by [[def-extended-real-valued-measurable-function]]. Since
$P(\{r=0\})=\int_{\{r=0\}}r\,dQ=0$ by
[[thm-likelihood-ratio-change-of-measure]], the value chosen there does not
affect $\int\ell\,dP$. Define
$$D(P\|Q):=\int \ell\,dP,$$
where $\log$ is the natural logarithm ([[def-natural-logarithm]]).

The definition is independent of the representative: two representatives
agree $Q$-almost everywhere, hence $P$-almost everywhere. Put
$$\psi(0):=0,\qquad \psi(t):=t\log t\quad(t>0).$$
The function $\psi$ is continuous at zero: for $s\ge1$,
$$0\le \frac{\log s}{s}=\frac1s\int_1^s\frac{du}{u}\le\frac1s\int_1^s\frac{du}{\sqrt u}\le\frac2{\sqrt s}.$$
Thus $t\log t\to0$ as $t\downarrow0$; here $L=\log$ by
[[cor-integral-logarithm-agrees-with-natural-logarithm]] and
[[def-integral-logarithm]]. On $(0,\infty)$, $\psi$ is a product of continuous
functions by [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]] and
[[thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions]], so $\psi$ is continuous on
$[0,\infty)$ and $\psi(r)$ is measurable by
[[def-extended-real-valued-measurable-function]]. Its signed integral is
defined by the positive and negative parts
([[def-positive-and-negative-parts-of-a-function]],
[[def-nonnegative-lebesgue-integral]]).

For $0<t\le1$, the function $-t\log t$ has derivative $-\log t-1$ and
maximum $1/e$ at $t=1/e$: $e=\exp(1)>1$ by
[[def-real-exponential-function-and-e]] and
[[thm-exponential-is-strictly-increasing]], $1/e=\exp(-1)$ by
[[cor-exponential-reciprocal-and-positivity]], and $\log(1/e)=-1$ by
[[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]] and the inverse definition. The mean value
theorem gives increase before and decrease after this point
([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-integral-logarithm-derivative-and-normalisation]],
[[cor-integral-logarithm-agrees-with-natural-logarithm]], [[cor-mean-value-theorem]]).
At $t=0$ the negative part is zero. Since $Q$ is a probability measure,
$$\int \psi(r)^-\,dQ\le\frac1e.$$
The change-of-measure identity of [[thm-likelihood-ratio-change-of-measure]],
applied to $\ell^-$ gives $\int\ell^-\,dP=\int\psi(r)^-\,dQ\le1/e$,
so $\int\ell\,dP$ is well-defined; applying it to both positive and negative
parts gives
$$D(P\|Q)=\int\ell\,dP=\int\psi(r)\,dQ=\int r\log r\,dQ,$$
with $0\log0:=0$ and a finite negative part. Therefore the extended integral
is well-defined without an $\infty-\infty$ ambiguity.

This convention is directional: the first argument must be absolutely
continuous with respect to the second for the integral formula to apply.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be an arbitrary measure space. Let $f,g:X\to[0,+\infty]$ be measurable. Then
$$\int g\,d(f\,d\mu)=\int gf\,d\mu.$$

Assume AC and use the directional convention of
[[def-kullback-leibler-divergence]]. For probability measures $P,Q$ on one
measurable space, $D(P\|Q)\ge0$, and $D(P\|Q)=0$ if and only if $P=Q$.

There is also the following normalized-density identity. Let
$(\mathsf X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a sigma-finite measure space: it is a set
with a sigma-algebra and measure ([[def-measure-space]]), and there is a
countable measurable cover by sets of finite $\mu$-measure
([[def-finite-sigma-finite-and-semifinite-measures]]). Let
$\gamma:\mathsf X\to[0,\infty)$ be a finite-valued measurable function with
$Z:=\int\gamma\,d\mu\in(0,\infty)$, and put $\pi=\gamma/Z$. Let
$q:\mathsf X\to[0,\infty)$ be a finite-valued measurable probability density,
so $\int q\,d\mu=1$, and suppose $q=0$ $\mu$-almost everywhere on
$\{\gamma=0\}$. Assume
$$ \int q\bigl(|\log\gamma|+|\log q|\bigr)\,d\mu<\infty, $$
where each term with $q=0$ is defined to be zero. Then
$$ \log Z =\int q(\log\gamma-\log q)\,d\mu +D(q\,\mu\|\pi\,\mu). $$
In particular, the first integral is at most $\log Z$. This identity concerns
normalized densities only; it does not assert posterior existence for an
unspecified statistical model.

**Inputs.** Supply a measurable parameter space $(\Theta,\mathcal T)$, sigma-finite measure spaces $(\mathsf X,\mathcal A,\nu)$ and $(\mathsf Z,\mathcal C,\mu)$, and a jointly measurable complete-data density $p(\theta,x,z)$ relative to $\nu\otimes\mu$ that integrates to one on each parameter fiber, as in [[def-latent-variable-joint-and-observed-data-factorization]]. This joint measurability is supplied explicitly and is not inferred from separate likelihood-density versions ([[def-likelihood-density]]). Also supply fixed observed data $x$, an initial value $\theta_0$, a mode `exact` or `generalized`, and a candidate selector that returns either a candidate or `unavailable` in finite time at each call. Require $0<m_{\theta_0}(x)<\infty$ and
$$
\int q_{\theta_0}^x(z)\,|\log p(\theta_0,x,z)|\,\mu(dz)<\infty.
$$

Write
$$
m_\theta(x):=\int_{\mathsf Z}p(\theta,x,z)\,\mu(dz),\qquad q_\theta^x(z):=\frac{p(\theta,x,z)}{m_\theta(x)}
$$
only when $0<m_\theta(x)<\infty$. By [[thm-observed-density-is-latent-marginal-under-tonelli]], $m_\theta$ is the observed-data density and $q_\theta^x$ is a probability density on every such fiber. The observed log likelihood is $\ell_x(\theta):=\log m_\theta(x)$ on those fibers.

At each valid iterate $\theta_t$, set $q_t:=q_{\theta_t}^x$ and define
$$
Q(\theta\mid\theta_t):=\int_{\mathsf Z}\log p(\theta,x,z)\,q_t(z)\,\mu(dz)
$$
only for candidates where this integral is finite. Use $\log0=-\infty$ and set $q_t|\log p|=0$ wherever $q_t=0$. The Q integral itself is choice-free. To test finite KL when $q_t\mu\ll q_\theta^x\mu$, assume AC as required by [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and [[def-kullback-leibler-divergence]]; when absolute continuity fails, $D=+\infty$ by that definition without AC. An **admissible candidate** $\theta$ also satisfies $0<m_\theta(x)<\infty$, $q_t\mu\ll q_\theta^x\mu$, and
$$
D(q_t\mu\|q_\theta^x\mu)<\infty,
$$
where the direction of $D$ is that of [[def-kullback-leibler-divergence]]. Require $\int q_t|\log p(\theta,x,\cdot)|\,d\mu<\infty$ for each candidate and $\int q_t|\log p(\theta_t,x,\cdot)|\,d\mu<\infty$ for the current iterate.

**Output.** Emit the iterate sequence beginning with $\theta_0$. If a stopping condition occurs after $T$ successful updates, return the finite list $(\theta_0,\ldots,\theta_T)$ and a status recording the first unavailable condition or selector result; do not append a failed candidate. If no stopping condition occurs, the emitted sequence is infinite and there is no finite stopping status.

**Procedure.** For $t=0,1,2,\ldots$, check that $0<m_{\theta_t}(x)<\infty$; if not, return the current list with status `stopped: invalid current marginal`. Form $q_t$ and $Q(\cdot\mid\theta_t)$ on admissible candidates. If $Q(\theta_t\mid\theta_t)$ is not finite, return with status `stopped: current Q is not finite`. Call the supplied selector. In **exact mode**, its candidate set must consist of admissible candidates and contain $\theta_t$; it returns an attained maximizer of $Q$ on that set, or `unavailable` if no attained maximum is available. In **generalized mode**, it returns any admissible $\theta_{t+1}$ with $Q(\theta_{t+1}\mid\theta_t)\ge Q(\theta_t\mid\theta_t)$, or `unavailable` if no such update is supplied. If the selector returns `unavailable`, return with status `stopped: no required update supplied`; otherwise append its candidate and continue. The procedure asserts no convergence or global-optimality property and makes no assertion for a candidate that loses current latent support.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ and $(Y,\mathcal B,\nu)$ be sigma-finite measure
spaces, and let $f : X \times Y \to [0,\infty]$ be product-measurable. Then
$x \mapsto \int_Y f_x\,d\nu$ and $y \mapsto \int_X f^y\,d\mu$ are measurable,
and

$$\int_{X \times Y} f\,d(\mu \times \nu) = \int_X \left(\int_Y f_x\,d\nu\right)d\mu = \int_Y \left(\int_X f^y\,d\mu\right)d\nu.$$

derivations.claim: By [F3], $q_t\mu$ and $q_\theta^x\mu$ are probability measures. The support assumption makes $p(\theta,x,z)>0$ for $q_t\mu$-almost every $z$.

Regard $(z,x)\mapsto p(\theta_t,x,z)$ as the transposed density on $\mathsf Z\times\mathsf X$. Tonelli's theorem [F12] and the normalization in [F1] make it a joint probability density. Apply [F4] with the supplied filler probability $q_t\mu$; on the valid fiber $x$ the conditional law of $z$ is exactly $q_t\mu$. The jointly measurable density is explicit in the hypotheses; [F2] does not supply such measurability for separate pointwise versions.

Define $r(z)=q_t(z)/q_\theta^x(z)$ where $q_\theta^x(z)>0$ and $r(z)=0$ otherwise. Absolute continuity gives $q_t=0$ $\mu$-almost everywhere on $\{q_\theta^x=0\}$. For every measurable $A\subseteq\mathsf Z$, [F9] gives $\int_A r q_\theta^x\,d\mu=\int_A q_t\,d\mu$, so $r$ is a Radon–Nikodym derivative of $q_t\mu$ with respect to $q_\theta^x\mu$. By [F8], $D(q_t\mu\|q_\theta^x\mu)=\int q_t(z)\log\frac{q_t(z)}{q_\theta^x(z)}\,\mu(dz)=Q(\theta_t\mid\theta_t)-Q(\theta\mid\theta_t)+\ell_x(\theta)-\ell_x(\theta_t)$, because $\log q_t=\log p(\theta_t,x,z)-\log m_{\theta_t}(x)$ and $\log q_\theta^x=\log p(\theta,x,z)-\log m_\theta(x)$ on the $q_t$-full support. The absolute integrability assumptions make these log integrals finite; rearranging proves the identity.

On a $q_t\mu$-full set, define $Y(z)=\log p(\theta,x,z)-\log p(\theta_t,x,z)$ and set $Y=0$ on its null complement. The assumptions make $Y$ integrable, and [given, step 1.1] gives $p(\theta,x,z)>0$ there. Using $q_t=p(\theta_t,x,\cdot)/m_{\theta_t}(x)$ from [F1], [F9] gives $E_{q_t}e^Y=m_{\theta_t}(x)^{-1}\int_{\{p(\theta_t,x,z)>0\}}p(\theta,x,z)\,\mu(dz)\le m_\theta(x)/m_{\theta_t}(x)$. This expectation is positive because $e^Y>0$ $q_t\mu$-almost everywhere, and finite by the displayed bound. Since $q_t\mu$ is the conditional law at $x$ by step 1.2, [F5]–[F6] give the scalar conditional expectations on the trivial sigma-algebra. The assumptions make $e^Y$ integrable, so [F7] with $\phi(y)=e^y$ yields $Q(\theta\mid\theta_t)-Q(\theta_t\mid\theta_t)=E_{q_t}Y\le\log E_{q_t}e^Y\le\ell_x(\theta)-\ell_x(\theta_t)$.

The divergence in step 1.3 is nonnegative by [F10] under [A1]. Thus the exact identity also yields the likelihood lower bound in step 2.1 and identifies its nonnegative gap; it does not identify parameter labels.

For an admissible generalized update the Q difference is nonnegative by its definition in [F11]. An attained exact maximizer over a set containing $\theta_t$ has Q at least $Q(\theta_t\mid\theta_t)$ for the same reason. Step 2.1 therefore gives $\ell_x(\theta)\ge\ell_x(\theta_t)$ in either case.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Let $(\Theta,\mathcal T)$, $(\mathsf X,\mathcal A)$, and
$(\mathsf Z,\mathcal C)$ be measurable spaces (sets equipped with
sigma-algebras; [[def-measurable-space]]). Let $\nu$ and $\mu$ be sigma-finite
reference measures on the observation and latent spaces; each has a countable
measurable cover by sets of finite measure
([[def-finite-sigma-finite-and-semifinite-measures]]). The finite product
sigma-algebra is generated by measurable rectangles
([[def-product-sigma-algebra-and-finite-product-sigma-algebras]]). The product
reference measure $\nu\otimes\mu$ is the one supplied by
[[thm-sigma-finite-product-measure-exists-is-rectangular-and-is-unique]].

A **jointly measurable latent-variable density** is a specified function
$$ p:\Theta\times\mathsf X\times\mathsf Z\longrightarrow[0,\infty] $$
measurable for $\mathcal T\otimes\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal C$ and normalized
on every parameter fibre:
$$ \int_{\mathsf X\times\mathsf Z}p(\theta,x,z)\, (\nu\otimes\mu)(d(x,z))=1\qquad(\theta\in\Theta). $$
Here $x$ is the observed coordinate and $z$ the latent coordinate. The
observed marginal density is
$$ m(\theta,x):=\int_{\mathsf Z}p(\theta,x,z)\,\mu(dz). $$
The valid-fibre set is
$V:=\{(\theta,x):0<m(\theta,x)<\infty\}$. Only on $V$ define the normalized
latent-fibre density
$$ q(z\mid\theta,x):=\frac{p(\theta,x,z)}{m(\theta,x)}. $$
This definition requires a single jointly measurable density as an input.
[[def-likelihood-density]] supplies neither a sigma-algebra on $\Theta$ nor
joint parameter measurability from separately specified likelihood sections;
the joint measurability above is an additional hypothesis. Because $p$ is
already supplied as one joint function, this definition uses no choice axiom.
It does not assert that AC can turn separately specified pointwise likelihood
versions into a jointly measurable version. No quotient or pointwise
conditional density is asserted on a zero or infinite marginal fibre.

Assume the hypotheses of
[[def-latent-variable-joint-and-observed-data-factorization]]. Then
$m(\theta,x)=\int p(\theta,x,z)\,\mu(dz)$ is jointly measurable in
$(\theta,x)$. For each fixed $\theta$, it is an observed-data probability
density: it is $\mathcal A$-measurable and
$$ \int_{\mathsf X}m(\theta,x)\,\nu(dx)=1. $$
Consequently $m(\theta,x)<\infty$ for $\nu$-almost every $x$. On every valid
fibre $0<m(\theta,x)<\infty$, $q(z\mid\theta,x)=p(\theta,x,z)/m(\theta,x)$ is
a measurable $\mu$-density of total mass one. Finally, if $h:\Theta\times\mathsf X\times\mathsf Z\to\mathbb C$ is product
measurable and
$\int |h(\theta,x,z)|p(\theta,x,z)\,d(\nu\otimes\mu)<\infty$ for a fixed
$\theta$, Fubini permits exchanging the latent and observed integrals of
$hp$. No exchange is claimed without this absolute integrability.

**Inputs.** Supply a measurable parameter space $(\Theta,\mathcal T)$, sigma-finite measure spaces $(\mathsf X,\mathcal A,\nu)$ and $(\mathsf Z,\mathcal C,\mu)$, and a jointly measurable complete-data density $p(\theta,x,z)$ relative to $\nu\otimes\mu$ that integrates to one on each parameter fiber, as in [[def-latent-variable-joint-and-observed-data-factorization]]. This joint measurability is supplied explicitly and is not inferred from separate likelihood-density versions ([[def-likelihood-density]]). Also supply fixed observed data $x$, an initial value $\theta_0$, a mode `exact` or `generalized`, and a candidate selector that returns either a candidate or `unavailable` in finite time at each call. Require $0<m_{\theta_0}(x)<\infty$ and
$$
\int q_{\theta_0}^x(z)\,|\log p(\theta_0,x,z)|\,\mu(dz)<\infty.
$$

Write
$$
m_\theta(x):=\int_{\mathsf Z}p(\theta,x,z)\,\mu(dz),\qquad q_\theta^x(z):=\frac{p(\theta,x,z)}{m_\theta(x)}
$$
only when $0<m_\theta(x)<\infty$. By [[thm-observed-density-is-latent-marginal-under-tonelli]], $m_\theta$ is the observed-data density and $q_\theta^x$ is a probability density on every such fiber. The observed log likelihood is $\ell_x(\theta):=\log m_\theta(x)$ on those fibers.

At each valid iterate $\theta_t$, set $q_t:=q_{\theta_t}^x$ and define
$$
Q(\theta\mid\theta_t):=\int_{\mathsf Z}\log p(\theta,x,z)\,q_t(z)\,\mu(dz)
$$
only for candidates where this integral is finite. Use $\log0=-\infty$ and set $q_t|\log p|=0$ wherever $q_t=0$. The Q integral itself is choice-free. To test finite KL when $q_t\mu\ll q_\theta^x\mu$, assume AC as required by [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and [[def-kullback-leibler-divergence]]; when absolute continuity fails, $D=+\infty$ by that definition without AC. An **admissible candidate** $\theta$ also satisfies $0<m_\theta(x)<\infty$, $q_t\mu\ll q_\theta^x\mu$, and
$$
D(q_t\mu\|q_\theta^x\mu)<\infty,
$$
where the direction of $D$ is that of [[def-kullback-leibler-divergence]]. Require $\int q_t|\log p(\theta,x,\cdot)|\,d\mu<\infty$ for each candidate and $\int q_t|\log p(\theta_t,x,\cdot)|\,d\mu<\infty$ for the current iterate.

**Output.** Emit the iterate sequence beginning with $\theta_0$. If a stopping condition occurs after $T$ successful updates, return the finite list $(\theta_0,\ldots,\theta_T)$ and a status recording the first unavailable condition or selector result; do not append a failed candidate. If no stopping condition occurs, the emitted sequence is infinite and there is no finite stopping status.

**Procedure.** For $t=0,1,2,\ldots$, check that $0<m_{\theta_t}(x)<\infty$; if not, return the current list with status `stopped: invalid current marginal`. Form $q_t$ and $Q(\cdot\mid\theta_t)$ on admissible candidates. If $Q(\theta_t\mid\theta_t)$ is not finite, return with status `stopped: current Q is not finite`. Call the supplied selector. In **exact mode**, its candidate set must consist of admissible candidates and contain $\theta_t$; it returns an attained maximizer of $Q$ on that set, or `unavailable` if no attained maximum is available. In **generalized mode**, it returns any admissible $\theta_{t+1}$ with $Q(\theta_{t+1}\mid\theta_t)\ge Q(\theta_t\mid\theta_t)$, or `unavailable` if no such update is supplied. If the selector returns `unavailable`, return with status `stopped: no required update supplied`; otherwise append its candidate and continue. The procedure asserts no convergence or global-optimality property and makes no assertion for a candidate that loses current latent support.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $p(\theta,x,z)$ be a jointly measurable normalized complete-data density as in [[def-latent-variable-joint-and-observed-data-factorization]], and fix observed data $x$. Put $m_\theta(x)=\int p(\theta,x,z)\,\mu(dz)$. Let $\theta_t$ and $\theta$ satisfy $0<m_{\theta_t}(x),m_\theta(x)<\infty$. Define $q_t(z)=p(\theta_t,x,z)/m_{\theta_t}(x)$ and $q_\theta^x(z)=p(\theta,x,z)/m_\theta(x)$. Assume
$$
q_t\mu\ll q_\theta^x\mu,\qquad \int q_t(z)\bigl(|\log p(\theta_t,x,z)|+|\log p(\theta,x,z)|\bigr)\,\mu(dz)<\infty,
$$
and $D(q_t\mu\|q_\theta^x\mu)<\infty$. Use $\log0=-\infty$ and set $q_t|\log p|=0$ wherever $q_t=0$. Then, with $Q(\theta\mid\theta_t)=\int q_t(z)\log p(\theta,x,z)\,\mu(dz)$,
$$
\ell_x(\theta)-\ell_x(\theta_t) =Q(\theta\mid\theta_t)-Q(\theta_t\mid\theta_t) +D(q_t\mu\|q_\theta^x\mu).
$$
Consequently, any admissible update with $Q(\theta\mid\theta_t)\ge Q(\theta_t\mid\theta_t)$ does not decrease $\ell_x$. An exact M-step has this property when its maximum is attained over an admissible candidate set containing $\theta_t$. No equality-of-parameter conclusion is asserted when the KL divergence is zero.

Under the hypotheses of [[thm-em-observed-log-likelihood-is-nondecreasing]] and [[thm-generalized-em-is-nondecreasing-under-q-ascent]], including AC, these are one-step inequalities for a fixed data fiber. They do not prove that the likelihood sequence is bounded, that parameter iterates converge, that a limit point is stationary, or that a stationary point is globally optimal. The exact M-step also requires an attained Q maximum; ascent itself does not supply one. The examples [[ex-em-likelihood-has-two-local-maxima]] and [[ex-gaussian-mixture-likelihood-unbounded-under-covariance-collapse]] exhibit tied maxima and an unbounded observed likelihood. These are limits of the stated ascent result, not additional convergence theorems.

derivations.claim: Since $0\le(\theta^2-1)^2\le9$ on $[-2,2]$, $1/4\le r(\theta)\le1/2$. Thus $p_\theta$ is nonnegative and sums to one over $(x,z)\in\{0,1\}^2$ for every $\theta$. The observed density at $x=1$ is $m_\theta(1)=r(\theta)$.

The squared term $(\theta^2-1)^2$ vanishes exactly at $\theta=\pm1$ and is positive elsewhere. Therefore $r(\theta)$, and hence the observed likelihood and log likelihood, have strict local maxima at those two distinct parameter values; both are global maximizers with equal value, so neither is a strict global maximum.

For every current value $\theta_t=\pm1$, the latent conditional law is uniform on $Z$. For any candidate $\theta$, $Q(\theta\mid\theta_t)=\log r(\theta)-\log2$, so its exact maximizer set is again $\{-1,1\}$. The algorithm therefore emits the infinite alternating sequence, which has no limit while its log likelihood is constant. This verifies the limitation described in [F5] without contradicting the one-step ascent result [F4].

Let $P,Q$ be probability measures on the same measurable space
([[def-probability-measure]]). Absolute continuity $P\ll Q$ has the convention
of [[def-absolutely-continuous-with-respect-to-a-positive-measure]]. If
$P\not\ll Q$, define $D(P\|Q)=+\infty$. If $P\ll Q$, assume AC
([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as in [[def-likelihood-ratio-as-rn-derivative]] and
let $r=dP/dQ$ be a finite-valued nonnegative measurable representative of its
Radon–Nikodym class; such a representative exists by
[[lem-radon-nikodym-density-of-a-finite-positive-measure-has-a-nonnegative-representative]].
On $\{r=0\}$ set $\ell=0$, and on $\{r>0\}$ set $\ell=\log r$. This
function is measurable: for $a\ge0$, $\{\ell>a\}=\{r>\exp(a)\}$, and for
$a<0$, $\{\ell>a\}=\{r=0\}\cup\{r>\exp(a)\}$, by the inverse and
monotonicity properties of the natural logarithm
([[def-natural-logarithm]], [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]). These are
measurable sets by [[def-extended-real-valued-measurable-function]]. Since
$P(\{r=0\})=\int_{\{r=0\}}r\,dQ=0$ by
[[thm-likelihood-ratio-change-of-measure]], the value chosen there does not
affect $\int\ell\,dP$. Define
$$D(P\|Q):=\int \ell\,dP,$$
where $\log$ is the natural logarithm ([[def-natural-logarithm]]).

The definition is independent of the representative: two representatives
agree $Q$-almost everywhere, hence $P$-almost everywhere. Put
$$\psi(0):=0,\qquad \psi(t):=t\log t\quad(t>0).$$

$$0\le \frac{\log s}{s}=\frac1s\int_1^s\frac{du}{u}\le\frac1s\int_1^s\frac{du}{\sqrt u}\le\frac2{\sqrt s}.$$

[[cor-integral-logarithm-agrees-with-natural-logarithm]] and
[[def-integral-logarithm]]. On $(0,\infty)$, $\psi$ is a product of continuous
functions by [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]] and
[[thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions]], so $\psi$ is continuous on
$[0,\infty)$ and $\psi(r)$ is measurable by
[[def-extended-real-valued-measurable-function]]. Its signed integral is
defined by the positive and negative parts
([[def-positive-and-negative-parts-of-a-function]],
[[def-nonnegative-lebesgue-integral]]).

maximum $1/e$ at $t=1/e$: $e=\exp(1)>1$ by
